item.research_question: How does substituting Cr with Al in CoCrFeNi high-entropy alloys affect the phase transformation, mechanical properties, wear resistance, and corrosion behavior?
item.processing_route: Mechanical alloying of elemental metal powders (purity >99.9%, particle size <25 µm) at 350 rpm for 40 h using a high-energy planetary ball mill (3 mm and 10 mm stainless steel balls, ball-to-material ratio 1:1); followed by spark plasma sintering at 1000 °C, 31.2 MPa pressure, and 15 min holding time.
item.test_conditions: Room temperature (25 °C) tensile testing at 2 mm/min; Vickers hardness with 10 kgf load for 10 s; friction and wear testing at 120 r/min, 10 N load, 600 s duration against GCr15 balls; electrochemical testing in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution at 25 °C with scanning from −400 mV to 400 mV at 2 mV/s.
key_findings: As Al content (x) increases from 0.1 to 0.5, the BCC phase weight percentage increases from 0% to 32.9%.
The ultimate tensile strength (UTS) increases from 702.01 MPa (x=0.1) to a maximum of 1163.14 MPa (x=0.5).
Elongation decreases from 43.01% (x=0.1) to a minimum of 26.98% (x=0.5).
The maximum Vickers hardness of 412.6 HV is achieved by Al0.5Cr0.5CoFeNi.
Al0.1Cr0.9CoFeNi exhibits the lowest friction coefficient of 0.513 and the lowest wear rate of 0.020 × 10−3 mm3/Nm.
Al0.5Cr0.5CoFeNi shows the highest self-corrosion potential (Ecorr) of 0.202 V in 3.5 wt.% NaCl solution.
The wear mechanism transitions from adhesive wear to a combination of adhesive and abrasive wear, and finally to oxidative wear as test time progresses.
item.mechanism: The increase in Al content, which has a larger atomic radius and more negative mixing enthalpy, induces atomic-level stress that drives the transformation of the FCC phase to the BCC phase. The presence of Cr-rich and Cr-poor phases creates a micro-electrical couple where the Cr-rich phase acts as a cathode and the Cr-poor phase as an anode, leading to selective corrosion. The BCC phase, having fewer slip systems than FCC, restricts dislocation movement, thereby increasing hardness and strength while reducing plasticity.
item.limitations: The authors state that the presence of Cr-rich and Cr-poor phases invariably results in selective corrosion, making the corrosion resistance weaker than that of a single-phase solid solution alloy with a similar composition that only undergoes pitting corrosion.
item.future_work: The authors propose that the influence of sintering temperature and pressure on microstructure and properties, as well as the effects of residual stress and metastable phases generated by the SPS process, will be the primary focus of subsequent research.
quotes: As the aluminum content increases, part of the FCC phase begins to transform to BCC.
The highest ultimate tensile strength of 1163.14 MPa is exhibited by Al0.5Cr0.5CoFeNi, while the minimum elongation is 26.98% and the maximum hardness value is 412.6 HV.
The presence of the Cr-rich and Cr-poor phases invariably results in selective corrosion in a neutral NaCl solution.
